subject: SI governance playbook — acceptance criteria and handover for regional on‑prem integrations
messages:
From: Lena Berg <lena.berg@innovateregs.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@innovateregs.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Regional SI engagement (EU/APAC) — initial ask

Hi Connor,

Thanks for taking time on the call today. Per our discussion, InnovateRegs is interested in becoming a certified regional SI for EU on‑prem/local deployments. To prepare our internal statements and pricing for the pilot, can you share Redwood's acceptance criteria for partner‑delivered on‑prem integrations (data residency controls, KMS integration, audit evidence, etc.)?

Specifically, we need a checklist we can use in our technical and commercial response:
- Exact evidence Redwood requires for data residency (system snapshots, logs, attestations)
- KMS/HSM integration expectations (API surface, key wrap vs. external keys)
- Required SOC 2 / pen‑test / vulnerability scanning artifacts and frequency
- Any required contractual addenda (DPA language, data processing terms)

We aim to propose a 6‑week pilot timeline and need to know whether that window looks feasible. I've attached a short proposed timeline and our commercial contact is copied.

Appreciate a short checklist we can use in our SOW.

Thanks,
Lena
——
Lena Berg
Head of Integrations, InnovateRegs

InnovateRegs — systems integrator for regulated workloads

Subject: Re: Regional SI engagement (EU/APAC) — initial ask

Hi Lena — great to meet today. High level: a 6‑week pilot can work for a scoped POC, but acceptance criteria must be met before customer cutover. I've pasted a concise partner acceptance checklist below and copied the delivery/runbook owners who will add operational detail.

Redwood partner acceptance checklist (summary):
1) Data residency verification
   - Signed DPA + locality clause for customer tenancy
   - Network diagram showing data flow boundaries (ingress, egress, backplane)
   - Proof of environment build in regional infra or air‑gapped network (screenshot / deployment manifest)
2) Key management
   - KMS integration doc (API endpoints, auth flow) or KMS attestation for customer‑managed keys
   - If HSM used, vendor and FIPS level noted; key custody model documented
3) Security evidence
   - Latest SOC 2 (Type II) or equivalent report; if not available, recent pen test report + remediation plan
   - Vulnerability scan report and scan cadence for customer images
4) Observability & audit logs
   - Retention policy and sample audit log export for review (token/trace level redacted)
   - Access control matrix showing who has admin access and break‑glass procedures
5) Runbook & support
   - Oncall handover doc, escalation matrix, and a 90‑day stabilization window with defined SLA exceptions for first month
   - Rollback plan and acceptance test cases for each cutover activity
6) Contracts & procurement
   - PO or SOW with explicit infrastructure ownership boundaries, liability language, and indemnities for data breaches linked to partner operations

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa will share the governance matrix and the runbook template we expect partners to fill out.
- Naomi will scope compliance evidence needed per account class (SMB vs enterprise).
- Soojin will follow up on quotas/throughput baselines Redwood will require for production traffic.

If you can return the attached POC timeline with dates adjusted to include an evidence review slot (week 2 of the pilot), we can confirm feasibility.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Partner Programs Manager
Redwood Inference

Lena / team — attaching the initial governance matrix and a runbook template we ask partners to complete as part of onboarding. I've included comments where we frequently see gaps. Summary of required deliverables (expanded):

A) Technical deliverables (must be submitted before customer staging):
  • Deployment manifests (Helm/YAML) and asset hashes for images
  • Network diagrams + firewall rule set (ingress/egress)
  • Proof of KMS integration: sample API call and successful key wrap/unwrap logs (redact secrets)
  • Encryption at rest verification and full disk encryption statement for local nodes

B) Compliance deliverables:
  • SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 cert OR recent third‑party pen test (<= 12 months) with remediation tickets
  • DPA signed and countersigned copy; any required addenda for cross‑border transfers
  • Evidence of background checks for engineers with admin access (summary statement, not PII)

C) Operational deliverables:
  • Oncall rota for the POC + a named handover engineer and escalation contacts (phone/mobile + backup)
  • 90‑day stabilization runbook: acceptance tests, traffic ramp schedule, error budgets and rollback criteria
  • Backups & retention policy docs (locations, restore test logs)

D) Commercial/procurement:
  • SOW with milestones tied to acceptance tests; invoice and payment terms for pilot fee
  • Insurance certificate covering operations in the region

Please see attached: si_governance_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix with pass/fail per item) and runbook-template.md. We've left the "acceptance test" column empty for your team to propose pass thresholds.

A couple of calls to request:
- Technical session the week of July 26 to review manifests and KMS integration.
- Contract alignment call (procurement) the week of Aug 2.

Connor, Naomi/Soogin — flagging this for your calendars.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Partner Enablement
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa, Connor — this is very helpful and much appreciated. A couple quick clarifications before we populate your templates: 

1) Data residency verification: for customer staging we can provide deployment manifests and signed attestations from our engineering lead. Is a screenshot/manifest plus a signed attestation acceptable, or do you require a live audit run against the environment?

2) KMS: we plan to support both customer‑managed KMS (customer key) and partner‑managed key wraps. For customer‑managed keys we can provide sample calls and a key wrap audit log. Are there specific auth flows Redwood requires (e.g., mTLS vs OAuth)?

3) SOC2 vs pen test: InnovateRegs does not yet have SOC2 Type II; we can provide a recent (May 2027) pen test and remediation report. Does Redwood accept pen test + remediation plan as a substitute for SOC2 for pilot customers?

We will populate the matrix this week. Also, we are happy to sign the DPA — please send the DocuSign link and we'll route it to our legal buyer.

Proposed pilot timeline (updated):
- Week 0: SOW & DPA sign (Aug 2)
- Week 1: Environment build + manifests submission
- Week 2: Evidence review and pen test verification
- Week 3–4: Staging acceptance tests + performance baseline
- Week 5: Customer cutover rehearsal (rollback test)
- Week 6: Go‑live window (soft launch)

If that aligns, we'll return a populated matrix and the procurement PO within 5 business days.

Regards,
Lena

Attachments: none inline (InnovateRegs-POC-timeline.pdf previously provided)
